clue.text: Digs for money in the US

explanation.surface: Someone excavates in search of cash in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs are lodgings, as are quarters; in America a quarter is a 25-cent coin, so quarters are money there.

clue.text: Ships built in Britain for a New York borough

explanation.surface: Vessels from British yards are named after a part of New York.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Cunard liners Queen Mary and Queen Elizabeth were British-built ships; Queens is also one of the five boroughs of New York City.

clue.text: Fine sort of race in which to find me

indicators.note: the clue says me is to be found inside the other letters, so it goes within them
a sort of race is a reshaped version of the word race, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A competitor wonders about a race that might suit them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges RACE to ARCE, and 'in which to find' puts ME inside it after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To amerce is an old legal verb meaning to punish with a monetary penalty, as to fine does.

clue.text: Small monkey with an old master

parts.note: a titi is a small South American monkey

explanation.surface: A little primate is pictured alongside a famous painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was a Venetian Renaissance painter, and an old master is a great European painter of that era.

clue.text: Introduces various price cuts

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of the word are taken in a different order

explanation.surface: A shop launches several discounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges the ten letters of INTRODUCES.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduction is a lowering of cost, so price cuts are markdowns.

clue.text: Vegetarian dishes for young Nazi storm-troopers?

parts.note: SA stands for Sturmabteilung, the Nazi brownshirt storm-troopers
young men are lads

explanation.surface: Meat-free meals are offered to junior members of a Nazi paramilitary.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'young Nazi storm-troopers' as SA LADS, youths of the SA.
explanation.definitionFit: Salads are cold mixed plates of leaves and raw vegetables, suitable for those who eat no meat.

clue.text: A talented artist rings a bell for her

indicators.note: rings means encircles, so the outer letters go round the next word

parts.note: ARA stands for Associate of the Royal Academy, a recognised artist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gifted painter sounds a bell to summon a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' puts BELL between ARA and the second A. 'her' defines a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabella is a female first name, and her stands for any woman.

clue.text: New Year gifts whose days are numbered

definitions.text: New Year gifts whose days are numbered

parts.words: New Year gifts whose days are numbered
parts.note: presents given at the turn of the year that list every date, and so are only useful for one year

explanation.surface: Presents at New Year that will soon be obsolete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whose days are numbered' usually means about to die; here the days are literally numbered on the pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearly calendar books listing dates, tides and events are traditionally sold or given at the year's start.

clue.text: Versatile danseuse of African nationality

indicators.note: versatile means turning readily to new forms, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An adaptable ballerina comes from a country in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Versatile' rearranges DANSEUSE, a female ballet dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes people from Sudan, a country in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Balanced sort of diet that comes rather late in the day

parts.note: balanced means level or even

indicators.note: a sort of diet is the word diet reshaped, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A healthy eating plan that only begins in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges DIET to TIDE, placed after EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, the closing part of daylight.

clue.text: Battered revolutionary with a couple of thousand tucked away

indicators.note: tucked away means stowed inside, so these letters go within the revolutionary

parts.note: a red is a communist revolutionary
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them is MM

explanation.surface: A bruised rebel has two thousand pounds hidden on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked away' puts A and MM inside RED, after its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Rammed means struck forcefully again and again, as battered does.

clue.text: Complete lack of opportunity for faultless batting?

explanation.surface: A cricketer bats so well that the fielders never get a chance.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a chance is a catch offered to the fielders; an innings without one is chanceless.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means not the slightest possibility; a batsman who gives the fielders no catchable ball has played without error.

clue.text: A standard author with no French following

indicators.note: following means the French word comes after the author

parts.note: pen stands for a writer, as in the pen name of an author
non is French for no

explanation.surface: A typical writer is pursued by a refusal from France.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'no French' as the French for no, NON.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long narrow flag, and a standard is a banner or flag.

clue.text: Quest'oquella rendered in English?

parts.note: the Italian words, from the Duke's aria Questa o quella in Verdi's Rigoletto, translated literally into English

explanation.surface: A line of Italian opera put into English.
explanation.walkthrough: The page runs the Italian words together; the aria title means one or another.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase translates word for word as a pair of alternatives, meaning one or the other.

clue.text: Mountain resorts in which VIPs predominate?

explanation.surface: Alpine holiday spots full of important people.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the idiom 'friends in high places', meaning in powerful circles.
explanation.definitionFit: Lofty locations are literally elevated; figuratively the phrase means positions of power where influential people gather.

clue.text: He'll make a song about artillery fire

indicators.note: about means around, so the singing goes round the other word

parts.note: to make a song is to sing
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A man will make a fuss in song about guns firing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts HELL (from He'll) inside SING, after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelling is bombardment with explosive projectiles from big guns.

clue.text: Free admission?

parts.note: entry for nothing, read as unrestricted access through an unlocked entrance

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark turns the phrase from ticket price to the policy of letting anyone in.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means unrestricted access or an unlimited immigration policy, so entry is not barred.

clue.text: Antoine's inordinately privileged pupils

indicators.note: inordinately means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the name with its possessive S

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's schoolchildren are excessively favoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inordinately' rearranges ANTOINES, the S of the possessive included.
explanation.definitionFit: Boys at Eton College, an exclusive English private school, are by reputation a privileged elite.

clue.text: The maximum length of a set square

definitions.text: The maximum length of a set square

parts.words: The maximum length of a set square
parts.note: a set square is a right-angled triangle used in drawing, and its longest edge is the side opposite the right angle

explanation.surface: How long is the biggest edge of a drawing instrument?
explanation.walkthrough: 'set square' sounds like a measurement of a square, but it is a triangular drawing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: In a right-angled triangle the longest side lies opposite the right angle.

clue.text: French city packed with Marines for the opera

indicators.note: packed with means filled with, so the marines go inside the city

parts.note: Caen is a city in Normandy
RM stands for Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A Normandy city is crowded with troops on opera night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packed with' puts RM inside CAEN, after CA.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmen is Bizet's opera about a Spanish gypsy.

clue.text: A Muslim who is lawfully employed

definitions.text: A Muslim who is lawfully employed

parts.words: A Muslim who is lawfully employed
parts.note: a Muslim scholar whose occupation is the teaching and interpretation of sacred law

explanation.surface: A Muslim with a legitimate job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lawfully employed' seems to mean in legal work; here the law is the religious law the scholar is employed to teach.
explanation.definitionFit: A mullah is a Muslim cleric trained in Islamic theology and sacred law.

clue.text: A container ship, possibly

explanation.surface: A box that might be a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is a receptacle such as a jug or bowl, and also any craft that sails, a ship being one example.

clue.text: Fish about in the inside of one's pocket, maybe

definitions.text: the inside of one's pocket, maybe

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fish goes round the next word

parts.note: ling is a long cod-like sea fish
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone rummages for something in their pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts IN inside LING, after the L. 'Fish about' reads as rummage, but Fish is the ling.
explanation.definitionFit: A lining is the inner layer of fabric in a garment, as found inside a pocket.

clue.text: Invaluable servant one would be lucky to find

definitions.text: one would be lucky to find

explanation.surface: A superb domestic helper is a rare discovery.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem of a helper or employee is called a treasure; buried riches are a lucky find.

clue.text: The places it links come under constant pressure

definitions.text: The places it links come under constant pressure

parts.words: The places it links come under constant pressure
parts.note: a weather-map line joining points where the barometric reading is the same

explanation.surface: The towns it connects are always being squeezed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under constant pressure' sounds like stress; on a weather chart it means equal atmospheric pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather chart such lines join places with equal barometric readings.

clue.text: But it isn't a terrible muddle in York!

definitions.text: But it isn't a terrible muddle in York!

parts.words: But it isn't a terrible muddle in York!
parts.note: a word for a chaotic mess is also the name of a famous medieval street in York, which is no mess

explanation.surface: Defending the historic city against a charge of chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shambles is a narrow medieval street of overhanging timber-framed houses in York, a city in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a total mess, and is also the name of a well-preserved old street in York.

clue.text: Gaudy hags cavorting round Rhode Island

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go about the state
cavorting means leaping about, so the letters of hags are jumbled

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Rhode Island

explanation.surface: Flashy old witches dance around an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavorting' rearranges HAGS to GASH, and 'round' puts it around RI, after GA.
explanation.definitionFit: Garish means showy and over-bright, as gaudy does.

clue.text: French-speaking writer from Shetland

indicators.note: from means the writer's name is made out of these letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: A Francophone author comes from the Scottish isles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' rearranges SHETLAND, the islands north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Stendhal was the pen name of Marie-Henri Beyle, a nineteenth-century French novelist.
